identity.hardware_model: BBC micro:bit v2 (diffdrive chassis, replacing vevav on the playfield)

connection._radio_note: Channel and group are derived from the board's name per radio-robot-lib docs/design/radio-addressing.md (channel 11 + n % 73, group 15 + n % 241; adopted 2026-09-13). Change only to resolve a name collision.
connection._v6_radio_link_note: 2026-09-06: tigez has NO WiFi module (no wifi_ip), so the v6 radio link over the relay is its only untethered carrier. pxt-nezha-diffdrive's make_deploy.py reads this key (_read_robot_radio_link) and boots the radio link in test.ts; without it the build defaults to OFF and a tigez placed on the field is unreachable -- MEASURED that day: firmware 1.20260906.7 built without it answered nothing to HELLO/PING/ID/STATUS through the relay on 55/114 while the camera showed it live on the field.

vision._note: MEASURED tigez 2026-08-30 (9-pose circle solve rms 0.18 cm) and CORRECTED 2026-08-31: the tag plates are REMOVABLE (top = robot front, bottom = back) and the 08-30 solve measured a mounting that sat ~90 deg off; +91.15 was that mounting's value, not the tag's. With the plate on correctly, -89.65 makes aprilcam report robot heading (verified: yaw reads true heading +-1 deg; 180-deg pivot wobble 0.50 cm, fieldtour6 session). The ~-90 all fleet tags carry cancels aprilcam's yaw convention (tag x-axis / paper-right), not a physical rotation. aprilcam registrations are IN-MEMORY PER-SESSION by design -- re-register at every session start, then probe-fit the heading offset with a ~12 cm drive before the first real leg (pxt-nezha-diffdrive reports/tigez-field-square-20260831.md).
vision._units_note: tag_offset_x/y/z are MILLIMETRES, the tag relative to the CENTRE OF ROTATION in the robot frame (x forward, y left). tag_offset_yaw is DEGREES and is the FULL mount yaw: -90 (AprilCam's fixed front-edge-to-hat convention, see pxt-nezha-diffdrive .claude/rules/tag-yaw-is-the-front-edge-not-the-hat.md) plus the physical plate residual. Feed it to the daemon as mount_yaw_rad; do NOT add the 90 again in your own code. Nothing read tag_offset_yaw as of 2026-09-05, so this fixes the convention: it matches tigez's previous non-schema tag_mount_yaw_deg -89.65, which was -90 + 0.35 residual.
vision._provenance: TIGEZ-MEASURED 2026-09-05 by pxt-nezha-diffdrive tests/calibration/mount.py on the SECONDARY playfield (110x70, camera hd-usb-camera): 9 rest poses over 8 +-90 pivots, rms 1.1 mm, verification drift 0.06 cm/pivot -- the tightest solve of the session. Heights are the stakeholder's tape measurements the same day. Artifact: reports/pf2-recal-20260905/08-mount-tigez/mount.json. Residual -3.77 deg from a 300 mm probe.

geometry._trackwidth_note: Renamed from trackwidth_mm 2026-09-16: the loader (src/host/rogo/config.py) and radio-robot-c's world_goto_chart._robot_geometry() both read geometry.trackwidth, so under the old spelling BOTH read None/their 126.0 default and this robot's correct value was invisible. Value itself unchanged and re-confirmed by stakeholder calipers 2026-09-16 (114.4), the only robot whose stored number already matched.
geometry._rotational_slip_note: 2026-09-16: surfaced to geometry.rotational_slip so the loader sees it (it previously returned None). Value is firmware_bake.rotational_slip, measured in tigez-turn-calibration-20260903.md; NOT re-measured here -- no independent effective-track figure exists for tigez.
geometry._note: MEASURED tigez 2026-08-30 on the playfield, camera-truthed: 80 cm run gave 800.9 mm camera vs 10184/10189 encoder tenth-degrees (L/R matched 0.05%); trackwidth from 8-pivot sweep (45..180 both directions); slip 0.992 trimmed live on fw 0.20260829.2 (gain 1.042 -> 0.986). Offset -0.83 deg/turn NOT folded into slip per the double-correction rule.

firmware_bake._note: MEASURED tigez 2026-09-03 on the playfield, camera-truthed, tests/playfield/turn_calibration.py, reports/tigez-turn-cal-20260903/: baseline (slip 0.952, overrun 0) over-rotated a flat +4.4 deg per pivot at 60 mm/s and +2.7 at the default cruise (~185 mm/s); overrun 5.5 mm + slip 0.96 (b_eff 119.0 mm at the 114.2 firmware default) centred the default-cruise sweep: 36 pivots of +-90/107/180, per-angle mean +0.8/+1.6/0.0 deg (06-confirm). slip here is 0.96 x 114.4/114.2 so b_eff is unchanged with the caliper trackwidth baked. Residual is speed dependent (end-of-pivot overrun grows with cruise): at 60 mm/s these values under-rotate 90s by ~2 deg. travel_calib from the 2026-08-30 80 cm run.
firmware_bake._stop_distance_provenance: UNVERIFIED on the sprint-029 engine, set 2026-09-04 by pxt-nezha-diffdrive when tigez was reflashed onto it. The previous key here was pivot_overrun_mm 5.5 -- the PRE-029 engine's post-target coast, measured camera-truthed (see the notes above) and superseded: 029's predictive arrival removes that coast by design (docs/design/motion-profile-unification.md S6.3), and tovez measured stop_distance 0 on it (captures/bench-acceptance-029-20260904d, pivot-gates Phase A). Baking the old coast into the new engine would under-rotate by about that much. Re-measure per design S10.2: lag_s first (WHEELS_V step, TLM FULL), then 10 floor-cruise pivots by camera for stop_distance_mm. lag_s measured 2026-09-04 (see _lag_provenance).
firmware_bake._lag_provenance: TIGEZ-MEASURED 2026-09-04 on the secondary playfield (camera 2, hd-usb-camera), firmware 1.20260904.4 (sprint 029 engine), over the torture radio relay with camera-only scoring (--no-tlm), pxt-nezha-diffdrive reports/turn-cal-029-20260904/tigez-*: lag 0 -> +4.3 deg mean over-rotation (7 pivots, fit offset +6.6; dance +3.6/+4.2/+6.1); lag 0.04 -> +0.7/-1.5/+1.9/-1.8 at 90/-90/180/-180 (offset +0.3, 8 pivots); lag 0.10 -> -1.1/-0.4/+0.5/+0.4 (offset -0.75, 8 pivots). 0.05 sits on the centred plateau. CONFIRMED the same night (tigez-09/10/12/13): 22 pivots at 0.05 mean abs 1.1 deg (offset -0.4), 14 at 0.10 mean abs 0.65 (offset -0.7), 400 mm straights within 4 mm at both; 0.05 kept as the most-measured mid-plateau value. Same knob and same direction as vevov's lag_s 0.04 (vevov.json); tigez's step-response lag was not measured (no straight path clear of the other robots).
firmware_bake._provenance_20260917: CALC-MEASURED 2026-09-17 on the alternating iron cross (playfield 4, arducam-ov9782-usb-camera), nezha-robot-template test/calibratec.ts, spin 70 deg/s. A spin measures ONLY the effective track b = trackwidth/rotational_slip -- trackwidth and slip are not separately observable, since every consumer reads their ratio -- so trackwidth stays Eric's caliper measurement of 2026-09-17 and the slip carries the scrub, per this repo's standing rule that a geometric measurement is never 'corrected'. calc's estimator needs neither the sensor lever arm nor a fixed centre of rotation: for a RADIAL sector boundary one sensor's consecutive crossings are 45 deg apart whatever its radius or lateral offset, and the eight sectors sum to 360 so a centring error cancels over a whole revolution. That is why it is preferred over the camera-pivot and stripe-edge methods it supersedes, both of which assume a centre that these robots do not hold. CAVEAT, unresolved: calc spins at ~73 mm/s per wheel while the camera turn calibrations ran at 60-188 mm/s, and tigez's own note below records that this residual is speed dependent -- so the ~1% spreads against the older numbers may be a real operating-point difference, not error. SLIP IS STORED TO 3 DECIMALS because the firmware holds no more: setConfigValue stores round(value*1000). RUNS: b = 11.808, 11.732, 11.792 cm, mean 11.777, sd 0.040 (0.34%, standard error 0.20%). slip = 11.44/11.777 = 0.9714 -> 0.971. Per-channel gap sd 1.7-3.7 deg; the robot walked ~0.25 cm/rev (the fleet best), measured by its own AprilTag between runs. Walk and per-channel sd track together across all three robots, so the sd is a readout of pivot quality, not of the hand-cut tape. This does NOT confirm either earlier number, it SPLITS them: this file's previous 0.9617 on the 114.4 caliper implies b 118.96 mm, while nezha-robot-template boot.ts's calt result was 116.47 mm -- a 2.1% disagreement with calc almost exactly halfway between. calc is preferred on the estimator grounds above, which matter most on tigez: its sensor bar is mounted ~7 deg skew and its 9 cm lever doubles calt's arcsin(d/r) sensitivity relative to gopiv's 17 cm.
